title: Diagnostic: @main vs Top-Level Code
hints: A program has one entry point; `main.swift`'s top-level code already is one.
Mark the struct with `@main` and remove the top-level `App.main()` call.
`@main struct App { static func main() { print("hello") } }`.
jsBridge: A program has exactly one entry point: either top-level code in `main.swift`, or a type marked `@main`. Node's entry is simply the file you run. SwiftUI apps use `@main struct MyApp: App`.

compass.q: Node's entry point is whatever file you run. What decides the entry point in a Swift executable?
